Some LoRA characters can work well together in this workflow IF they require trigger words. This will help keep them from influencing each other too much. For full separation of LoRA model areas, see my Region LoRA workflow
Most important here are descriptions of poses, interactions, framing and perspective
Mute this (ctrl+m) once you have a good starting image

This workflow achieves increased control over composition, especially in regards to character interaction with fine control over each character by first generating an image with the desired composition, running a ControlNet OpenPose Preprocessor on it to extract the character poses and then generating a new image using the poses from the first one while also setting separate prompts to each character with latent couple.

#############################################################################
 ---------------------------------HOW TO USE---------------------------------
#############################################################################
(You will get a some errors using this workflow, it's just a part of how it works)

 1) Generate images in Group I for a desired composition, cancel after you hear a ping. You can also right-click group I -> set group nodes to never instead
 2) once you find a good one, mute 1st Pass in Group I (ctrl+m) or mute the whole group by right-click -> set group nodes to never and go to Group II 
 3) queue once and wait until you get an error, ignore it. The OpenPose Preprocessor will extract pose data from the generated image. See if it did a good job and start over if not, otherwise move on to step #4
 4) right-click on subject node -> Open in MaskEditor -> draw mask (do this for every subject)
 5) after all masks are done, queue and then cancel after visualisation of the drawn masks appears. If images update to something wrong, just repeat this step second time.
 6) The visualization will show you how all the masks look together, you can refine them as much as you like
 7) to finally generate an image, simply queue without cancelling

- Sometimes you need to queue and cancel twice to see effects (eg. after drawing masks)
- when in MaskEditor: scroll resizes the brush and right-click erases the mask

#############################################################################
 -----------------------------------OTHER-----------------------------------
#############################################################################
- If the ControlNet Preprocessor does a mostly fine job, but there are some details that it got wrong or if there are additional unwanted characters in the background it detected, you can mask parts of the image in the OpenPose Preprocessor group node to erase them from the image passed for ControlNet

- While you can control the background with the Background group node, you can also use subject nodes with ControlNet Strength set to 0 for finer control over location of background details

ControlNet slows down generation and here it is applied to the background and each subject independently. This slow down is especially noticeable in higher resolutions. It is recommended to remove it here unless you're using very high denoise in 2nd Pass
For me it went up from ~35s/it to over 100s/it with just 2 subjects in 2nd pass
Generated image will be the same size as input image
set seed or cfg to 0 (and control after generate to fixed for seed) to use the setting from 1st Pass
